value: search-phase peak frequency mean 55.2 kHz (SD 2.4, n = 9 bats, 715 search calls; trawling prey from water)
structure: echolocation call (search-phase call of a foraging bat in a flight cage)
measurement: peak frequency [kHz] (frequency at maximum amplitude), mean ± SD, Table 1 row 'Peak frequency [kHz]', habitat 'Water', column 'Search' (columns Search, Approach, Terminal phase FM/S/L)
method: Materials and Methods (as returned by the page reader): 'Over a period of 6 months (January–June 2003) we studied foraging and echolocation behavior of M. macrophyllum'; 'For behavioral experiments we caught nine adult (four females, five males) M. macrophyllum at a known roost site'; bats were flown in a flight cage (4.5 m × 4.5 m × 2 m) inside the forest of Barro Colorado Island, Panama, with prey suspended in the air or on the water surface of a basin (3 m × 2 m); calls were picked up by an ultrasound microphone, digitized at 312.5 kHz, 16 bit, recorded at 1/15 of original speed; spectrograms FFT 512 points, Hamming window, frequency resolution 646 Hz; peak frequency defined as 'frequency at maximum amplitude'; 'Measurements were taken at the point where call energy clearly exceeded background noise.' Statistics: 'we used mean parameter values per individual of the two chosen sequences for statistical analysis to avoid pseudoreplication' and 'For all statistical tests we used individuals as a statistical unit'. These sentences were returned by a page reader, not read verbatim on the page by me.
conditions: Search-phase calls of captive-flown wild-caught adults in a flight cage on Barro Colorado Island, Panama. Table 1 note: the water rows rest on '715 search calls, 1610 approach calls, and 360 terminal phase calls of nine bats'; the air rows on '278 search calls, 579 approach calls, and 128 terminal phase calls of eight bats hawking tethered mealworms'. The table does not say whether the mean ± SD is over calls or over per-bat means. Results as returned by the reader: 'we found no differences in echolocation call parameters between aerial or trawling prey captures' (two-factorial Anova, Tukey post-hoc, all p > 0.06, df = 69; the statement is about the call parameters generally, not peak frequency alone); 'echolocation calls in the field were always emitted at lower peak frequencies than in the flight cage' (field row in Table 1: search 54.4 ± 1.7 kHz from 11 field sequences, approach 51.9 ± 3.1 marked with an asterisk); the reader also returned that search-call peak frequency was 'slightly higher in experiments with dead mealworms (55.9 kHz)'. Same row also holds approach and terminal-phase (F, M, S, L) columns, not filed here. Habitat 'Water': bats taking prey from the water surface (trawling).
